sources.title: Steven Weinberg, Non-Renormalization Theorems in Non-Renormalizable Theories
sources.locator: Full 13-page PDF retrieved. Read equations (1)–(3), printed pp. 2–3, for the local Wilsonian action; read the complete spurion, R-charge, theta-shift, and graph-counting proof, equations (1)–(12), printed pp. 2–7. The prose case enumeration after equation (12) appears inconsistent for C_2; the count equation permits one C_2 vertex and the current local proof derives that case directly.

searches.query: site:arxiv.org/pdf/hep-th/9803099 Weinberg Non-Renormalization Theorems in Non-Renormalizable Theories
searches.outcome: Found the official arXiv full PDF; independently downloaded and extracted all 13 pages and read the complete relevant Wilsonian argument.

contents.name: Rigid N=1 Wilsonian action and F/D distinction
contents.support: Equations (1)–(3), printed pp. 2–3, specify the local superspace action with a gauge-invariant holomorphic chiral integrand, a separate real D-term, and a Wilsonian cutoff.

contents.name: Formal perturbative Wilsonian F-term theorem
contents.support: Equations (3)–(12), printed pp. 2–7, give the chiral/real spurion restrictions, R-charge and theta-shift arguments, and graph count. The C_2=1 case is taken from equation (12), not the conflicting prose enumeration.

sources.title: Stephen P. Martin, A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.locator: Full 160-page PDF retrieved. Read §4.7, printed p. 41, for the superspace action and chiral superfield equation of motion; §4.10, printed pp. 49–50, for general holomorphic superpotential and real Kähler/gauge-kinetic data; §5.1, printed pp. 52–53, for positive-mass-dimension soft trilinears; §6.5, printed pp. 66–67, for anomalous dimensions and canonical-coupling running; and §7.6, printed pp. 82–83, for chiral spurion extraction.

searches.query: site:arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/9709356v7 Stephen P Martin Supersymmetry Primer
searches.outcome: Found the author's version-7 full lecture notes; retrieved the complete PDF and inspected the superspace action, nonrenormalizable EFT, soft-term, RG, and spurion sections.

contents.name: Local rigid N=1 Wilsonian superspace action
contents.support: §§4.7 and 4.10 specify chiral superspace actions and the distinction between holomorphic superpotential/gauge terms and real Kähler data.

contents.name: Holomorphic superpotential versus canonical running
contents.support: §6.5 relates superpotential beta functions to field anomalous dimensions; it warns that canonical parameters can run even when the Wilsonian holomorphic coefficients do not.

contents.name: Leading heavy chiral equation and derivative correction
contents.support: §4.7 equations (4.7.5)–(4.7.9) derive the chiral action and superfield Euler equation, including the supercovariant-derivative term.

contents.name: Chiral spurion soft scalar trilinear
contents.support: §5.1 classifies scalar cubics with positive mass-dimension coefficients as soft terms; §7.6 equations (7.6.1)–(7.6.5) extracts component terms after fixing a chiral spurion background.

sources.title: Aneesh V. Manohar, Introduction to Effective Field Theories
sources.locator: Full 94-page Les Houches lecture notes retrieved. Read Chapter 5, §§5.5–5.7, printed pp. 38–41, for finite-order matching and the low-energy expansion; read Chapter 7, §§7.1–7.2, printed pp. 58–61, for decoupling and threshold matching.

searches.query: Aneesh Manohar Introduction to Effective Field Theories 1804.05863 Les Houches lecture notes arXiv
searches.outcome: Found the official arXiv full lecture notes (2017 Les Houches lectures, posted 2018); retrieved the complete 94-page PDF and read the cited matching and threshold sections.

contents.name: Finite operator truncation and coefficient matching
contents.support: Chapter 5 separates matching terms from low-energy contributions at a declared operator order; the local definition supplies the supersymmetric field and coefficient data.

contents.name: Heavy threshold and low-energy Wilsonian coefficient
contents.support: Chapter 7 presents threshold corrections and higher-dimension terms from a specified ordinary-QFT model; it does not derive a supersymmetric superpotential formula.

contents.name: EFT applicability qualification
contents.support: The fixed EFT expansion and scale hierarchy motivate the explicit finite-order model regime; the spurion component is calculated locally.

sources.title: C. P. Burgess, Introduction to Effective Field Theory
sources.locator: Full 55-page review retrieved. Read §§2.2.1–2.2.2, printed pp. 21–22, for Wilson-action mode separation and cancellation of the arbitrary intermediate scale; read §4.1.4, printed pp. 44–47, for electron/muon threshold matching.

searches.query: C P Burgess Introduction to Effective Field Theory hep-th/0701053 arXiv review
searches.outcome: Found the official arXiv full review and its version-of-record citation; retrieved the complete 55-page PDF and read the cited Wilson-action and threshold sections.

contents.name: Wilson-action scale and locality context
contents.support: §§2.2.1–2.2.2 describe high/low mode separation and the cancellation of the arbitrary intermediate scale in observables; no SUSY action is imported.

contents.name: Threshold-matching context
contents.support: §4.1.4 gives the ordinary-QED muon threshold example; the exact chiral coefficient formula is proved locally.

sources.title: Juan Carlos Criado and Manuel Pérez-Victoria, Field redefinitions in effective theories at higher orders
sources.locator: Full 42-page PDF retrieval reused from current run evidence. Read §2, PDF pp. 6–8, equations (2.2)–(2.8), for regulated changes of variables, Jacobians, transformed sources and LSZ; read §3 and §5.1 for higher-order EOM limitations and Appendix B, pp. 33–34, equations (B.1)–(B.11), for multiple EOM insertions.

contents.name: Conditional regulated field-redefinition and LSZ equivalence
contents.support: §2 and Appendix B support only the exact change-of-variables/Jacobian/source and stable-pole LSZ assumptions stated in the linked full-AC supplier; no unrestricted off-shell equivalence is imported.
